info.title: BankingAI API
info.description: Spending assistant backend on synthetic bank data. Every figure is computed here; a model only chooses tools and explains results. All endpoints except health and login need a bearer token.

get.summary: Every account of the customer as a plain array, oldest first
get.description:
`GET /api/accounts`: every account of the customer as a plain array, oldest first; `[]` when
there are none. No paging: a customer has only a handful of accounts.

401.description: No valid token (unauthorized) or the customer no longer exists (session_invalid).

post.description:
`POST /api/accounts`: opens a personal, zero-balance account for the customer and answers 201 with
its `Location` and the account exactly as `GET /api/accounts/{id}` returns it.

`GET /api/analytics/upcoming-payments`: the recurring payments expected in the next `days` days (1–31,
default 30; decision K3-A), earliest first, with overdue ones flagged and an estimated total per currency. Dates
and amounts are estimates from the recurring rule, never promises (ANA-12).

get.summary: This month's spending against a budget given by the user (never stored)
get.description:
`GET /api/analytics/budget-check`: this month's spending against a budget given by the user (never stored):
spent, remaining or over, daily average and a linear month-end projection whose method is named in the answer.
Without `categoryCode` and `merchant` the budget covers total spending; `currencyCode` is required
(ANA-13).

get.summary: "what if I cut it by N %?"
get.description:
`GET /api/analytics/savings-simulation`: "what if I cut it by N %?". The average of the last `months`
complete months (default 6, months without spending included) times the rate, per month and per year, one row per
currency; the assumption is named in `method`. Not investment advice: no return, interest or inflation (ANA-14).

get.description:
`GET /api/accounts/{accountId}/transactions`: a page of the account's transactions, newest first.
Either a symbolic period or both from and to
(local dates, inclusive); neither means the last three months. Another customer's account is a 404.

post.summary: Adds a synthetic Purchase or Salary to one of the customer's accounts and…
post.description:
`POST /api/accounts/{accountId}/transactions`: adds a synthetic Purchase or Salary to one of the
customer's accounts and answers 201 with its `Location` and the transaction exactly as
`GET /api/transactions/{id}` returns it. Needs an `Idempotency-Key`: the same key again returns
the first answer. A balance that would leave its range, or a key reused for another request, is a 409;
another customer's account is a 404.

409.description: The balance would leave its range (balance_limit) or the key was used for another request (idempotency_conflict).

get.summary: Searches all of the customer's accounts (a Business shop account included) like…
get.description:
`GET /api/transactions`: searches all of the customer's accounts (a Business shop account included) like a
statement, newest first, with optional filters: kind, direction, category or only unclassified purchases, merchant
(matched against the customer's own merchants, never guessed), one account, a currency and an inclusive amount
range in it (ANA-11). Without a period the last three months are searched, like an account's list (decision
K1-B); the answer names its period.

AccountDto.description:
An account as clients see it. The owner is deliberately absent: it is always the caller (taken from the
token), so it is never sent and clients are never tempted to send it back.

AssistantFact.description: One backend figure the answer is based on, already formatted for people ("Toplam harcama" / "145,00 TL").

message.description: 1–500 characters, not only whitespace; the same limit as the AI service.

AssistantMessageRequest.description:
Body of `POST /api/assistant/messages`: only the user's text. The customer comes from the token; any other
field (for example `customerId`) is a 400.

AssistantReply.description:
Reply of `POST /api/assistant/messages`. The figures in `answer` come from `facts`, which the
backend computed; the model only chose the tool and wrote the sentence.

AssistantReplyType.description: What kind of reply the assistant gave to one message.

AssistantStatus.description: Reply of `GET /api/assistant/status`: whether the chat screen can take questions right now.

arguments.description: The checked arguments, for example `period = Yesterday`.

AssistantToolCall.description:
A backend query the assistant ran for the answer, with the arguments it used, so the client can show how the
answer was found (AI-11) or link to the matching screen (CHAT-07).

BudgetCheck.description:
Result of BudgetCheckService. `Figures` is null only when a merchant text did not match exactly one
of the customer's merchants; `MerchantMatch` then says why. No spending is a real 0, not a missing answer.

accountName.description: 1–100 characters, not only whitespace (same rule as the database).

currencyCode.description: Exactly one of the account currencies the database accepts; "try" is not corrected.

CreateAccountRequest.description:
Body of `POST /api/accounts` (API-07). Holds only what the client may choose; owner, number, type
(always Personal), balance (always 0), id and creation time are set by the backend. Any other field in
the JSON is a 400 instead of being silently ignored.

oneOf.description:
`Purchase` (money out) or `Salary` (money in, so new zero-balance accounts can be used).
Two-legged kinds (Transfer, Sale) and OpeningFunding are not accepted.

amount.description: Positive, at most two decimals, within the money ceiling; never rounded.

description.description: The raw statement text, 1–500 characters, not only whitespace.

merchant.description:
Optional shop name, part of the event like on a card statement (1–150 characters). The category, the
bank's interpretation, is never taken from the client.

CreateTransactionRequest.description:
Body of `POST /api/accounts/{accountId}/transactions` (API-11): only the event itself. The backend
derives direction from the kind and currency from the account, takes the account from the URL and the time
from its own clock, and owns every category field; any of those in the JSON is a 400.

CurrencyRecurringTotal.description: Sum of the latest amounts: what the customer currently pays per month in one currency.

CurrencyUpcomingTotal.description: Sum of the estimated amounts in one currency.

status.description: `ok` when the database is reachable, otherwise `unavailable`.

database.description: Whether a connection to PostgreSQL could be opened.

HealthResponse.description: Liveness and database reachability of the API.

LoginRequest.description: Body of `POST /api/auth/login`. Both fields are required; a missing or blank one is a 400.

LoginResponse.description: A successful login: the bearer token and the moment it stops being accepted.

MeResponse.description:
`GET /api/me`: who the token belongs to. The internal customer id is deliberately left out; clients
never need it because every request is scoped by the token.

code.description: Fixed machine code, e.g. validation_failed, session_invalid.

errors.description: Only on validation_failed: client field name → Turkish messages.

Problem.description: Every error answer (API-13): a Turkish title, a fixed machine code and a trace id; never internals.

RecurringPattern.description:
Why a group counts as recurring: how many payments, their amount range and day gaps.
`NextExpectedDate` is an estimate (last payment + one month), never a promise.

RecurringPayment.description:
One recurring payment. The category comes from the group's latest payment;
`Pattern` explains why it counts as recurring.

RecurringPayments.description:
Result of RecurringPaymentService: the examined period, the recurring payments
(largest latest amount first) and the monthly total per currency.

SavingsSimulation.description:
Result of SavingsSimulationService: the complete months used (`From`–`To`), the assumption in
`Method` and one row per currency with spending in those months (none: empty list). A merchant text that does not
match exactly one of the customer's merchants gives no rows; `MerchantMatch` says why. `CategoryDisplayName`
is the category's Turkish name (MCP-18), as in BudgetCheck.

TransactionPage.description:
One page of an account's transactions: the resolved period, how many transactions it holds, whether more
pages follow, and the items (the shared TransactionItem, newest first).

UpcomingPayment.description:
One expected payment. Date and amount are estimates: the date is the recurring rule's next expected date (last
payment + one month on its usual day) and the amount is the latest payment's. `IsOverdue` marks an expected
date that has passed without a payment yet; `DaysUntil` is then negative. `Pattern` is the evidence.

UpcomingPayments.description:
Result of UpcomingPaymentService: the window `From` (today) – `To` (today + days, inclusive),
the expected payments (earliest first, overdue ones included) and the estimated total per currency.
